## What it is

WordPress builds and runs websites and blogs, with themes, plugins and an editor in the browser ([wordpress.org](https://wordpress.org); source mirror [WordPress/WordPress](https://github.com/WordPress/WordPress)).

**Licence:** `GPL-2.0-or-later` (`license.txt` at tag 7.1.4: "either version 2 of the License, or (at your option) any later version"). GitHub reports `NOASSERTION`, so the licence gate relies on the license-matrix row "WordPress". Market class **L2**. The image is the Docker Official Image `wordpress`, built by [docker-library/wordpress](https://github.com/docker-library/wordpress), not by the WordPress project itself.

**Icon:** a neutral generated icon with initials; no upstream logo or trademark is shipped.

## How it runs here

- One `Deployment` (`Recreate`) with WordPress (Apache and PHP 8.4) and MariaDB 11.8 LTS as a native sidecar bound to 127.0.0.1, so no other pod can reach the database.
- The database password is generated once by an init container onto the database volume and read through `MARIADB_PASSWORD_FILE` and `WORDPRESS_DB_PASSWORD_FILE`. The MariaDB root password is generated the same way into a folder that only the database container mounts (`MARIADB_ROOT_PASSWORD_FILE`); the image's `MARIADB_RANDOM_ROOT_PASSWORD` option is not used because it prints the password to the container log. WordPress's own secret keys are generated by the image when it writes `wp-config.php`.
- Non-root: WordPress as `www-data` (UID 33) and MariaDB as UID 999. Apache listens on port 80 through the namespaced sysctl `net.ipv4.ip_unprivileged_port_start=0`, which affects this pod only. No privilege escalation, all capabilities dropped.
- Volumes: `wordpress-html` (10 GiB, `/var/www/html`) and `wordpress-db` (5 GiB).
- Probes: `GET /` (302 to the installer before setup counts as healthy); MariaDB uses the image's `healthcheck.sh`.

## First run

Source: [WordPress "Installing WordPress"](https://developer.wordpress.org/advanced-administration/before-install/howto-install/), step "Run the install script".

1. Install WordPress from the Market and approve the action. It installs into `app-wordpress`.
2. Forward the port and open http://localhost:8080:
   ```sh
   kubectl -n app-wordpress port-forward svc/wordpress 8080:8080
   ```
3. Run the install wizard right after install (language, site title, admin user and password): whoever reaches it first becomes the admin.
4. WordPress stores the address you used (here `http://localhost:8080`) as the site URL. When the box gets a LAN name or HTTPS, change it in Settings, General.

## Not done yet

- No HTTPS or LAN hostname: OneMind v0 has no ingress or certificates for apps, so the site is reached through a port-forward until the app proxy exists. A public website also needs the exposure step (TAXONOMY §3.1, `public` needs its own approval).
- No email (SMTP): password reset and notification mails are not sent.
- WP-Cron runs on page visits (WordPress default); no system cron.
- `readOnlyRootFilesystem` is not set: it has not been tested against this image.
- Resource figures are OneMind choices; upstream publishes none for containers. They are checked against real use when the CI smoke test (contract §9.4 check 9) runs.
- `metadata.tier` stays `community` until `sdk/tools/app-gate` in CI writes a passing `scan.json`. `spec.updates.automerge` is `none` until `renovate.json` lists the app.

## Why this app is blocked

The CI app gate (`sdk/tools/app-gate`, contract §9.4) computed tier **blocked** for this app on 2026-11-12 (ci-apps run 43212771377, job `gate (wordpress)`). The gateway lists a blocked app in the Market but refuses to install it (§10.3, §11.1). The app is kept, not hidden, and the gate was not weakened. Reasons from that run:

- Vulnerability: `docker.io/library/mariadb:11.8.9-noble`: CVE-2025-68121 in the Go `stdlib` v1.24.6, fixed in 1.24.13, 1.25.7 or 1.26.0-rc.3.
- Recorded only (no fix available): wordpress image CVE-2026-119618 (apache2) and CVE-2026-6653 (libxml2).
- Passed: licence (matrix row for WordPress matches), ClamAV (0 infected), smoke test (GET / returned 302).

To unblock: move the pins to upstream releases that fix these findings (tags that exist, checked with `crane`), then rerun `sdk/tools/app-gate` (the daily `apps-rescan` workflow does this too). Nothing is bumped to an unverified tag.
